question: Organophosphate insecticides (such as malathion) exert their toxic effect by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, leading to accumulation of acetylcholine at nerve synapses.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Organophosphates inhibit acetylcholinesterase → accumulation of acetylcholine → cholinergic crisis (SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI distress, Emesis). Antidote: atropine (blocks muscarinic effects) + pralidoxime (reactivates AChE if given early).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Organophosphates irreversibly (or pseudo-irreversibly) inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine and resulting in the SLUDGE/DUMBELS syndrome — the basis for atropine + pralidoxime treatment.
